findings.summary: Post's tolerance does not tell an fp32 softmax from a half-precision one: at BLOCK_SIZE = 2^14 this kernel with its output rounded to float16 meets Post on every covered instance
findings.detail: Post bounds each output by relTol(BLOCK_SIZE)·σ + absTol, with relTol B = (B + 4)·2^-22 and absTol = 2^-22 fixed. Evaluated at the covered sizes (the benchmark's 4096 × N, N up to 12672, BLOCK_SIZE up to 2^14): (1) relTol(B) exceeds float16's unit roundoff 2^-11 for every B ≥ 2^11 (benchmark N ≥ 1152) and bfloat16's 2^-8 at B = 2^14 (16388·2^-22 = 0.0039072 > 0.0039063), so the correctly rounded float16 (resp. bfloat16) softmax meets Post there. (2) A concrete wrong kernel: the same source with `softmax_output.to(tl.float16).to(tl.float32)` stored at line 109. Its fp32 part has this claim's own worst-case error (sum_rel's (13B + 20)·2^-26, final_bound's hD, DivFull), and one float16 rounding adds 2^-11·|c| + 2^-25; at B = 2^14 the total, 0.003675·σ + 1.5·10^-7, is within relTol·σ + absTol (0.003907·σ + 2.4·10^-7), so that kernel meets Post on every covered instance, i.e. on every benchmark row with N ≥ 8320. (3) absTol alone admits a float16 rounding of every output σ ≤ 2^-11 ≈ 4.9·10^-4, which on the benchmark's larger rows is most of them (at N = 12672 a typical randn output is σ ≈ 4.8·10^-5, whose float16 rounding error, ≤ 2.3·10^-8, is a tenth of absTol = 2.4·10^-7); and in the covered row [20, 0, …, 0] (n_cols = 12672) the small outputs are σ ≈ 2.06·10^-9, absTol/116, so Post accepts 0 for them although the kernel computes them to a few ulps. (4) The source's own test (line 190, torch.allclose: rtol 1e-5, atol 1e-8) asks for agreement 24 times tighter than Post at its BLOCK_SIZE 1024. The part of the bound that grows with B is the row sum's (the library's reduction along any tree of depth up to B − 1), and it scales every output of a row by one common factor; the per-element errors (the subtraction, tl.exp, the division) do not grow with B, and the lanes' absolute error is relative to the row's largest lane (lane_facts: 2^-22·a + 2^-23 with a ≤ 1 = the max lane), i.e. 2^-23·max_k σ_k after the division by A, not 2^-23. What would resolve it: state each row's error as a common factor plus a per-element part, e.g. ∃ s, |s − 1| ≤ ρ(B) ∧ ∀ j < n_cols, |c_j − s·σ_j| ≤ ε·σ_j + η·max_k σ_k, with ε, η a few 2^-22 not growing with B (the existing lemmas lane_facts, sum_rel and DivFull's bound give these pieces), so that Post rejects an output rounded to float16 on some covered instance at every covered BLOCK_SIZE; or argue, with the kernel's use, why a half-precision result should count as meeting the specification of this float32 kernel.
findings.evidence: work/Check.lean (Lean-checked: 2^-8 < relTol(2^14), 2^-11 < relTol(2^11), 24·10^-5 < relTol(2^10), 2^-8·2^-14 ≤ absTol); work/tolerance.py (exact arithmetic of points 1–4 with the claim's constants).

findings.summary: The benchmark's first launch per call runs on a fresh stream (lines 217-218) not ordered after the torch.randn writing x on the previous stream: say that scope point 1 is assumed there
findings.detail: In benchmark (lines 215-226), x = torch.randn(…) (line 216) runs on the stream that is current when the call starts; lines 217-218 then create a new stream and make it current, and softmax(x) (line 222, via do_bench) launches the kernel on it. Nothing in lines 216-222 orders the new stream after the old one or synchronises: from the second call of benchmark on, randn runs on the stream the previous call created, and the kernel on another, so unless do_bench synchronises before it first calls its function, that first launch may start while randn still writes the claim's input x. That is Compiler.Faithful's scope point 1 (part B, nothing else writes the launch's bytes), which TVA assumes and nobody checks, so the claim's Lean is not affected; but the README's Conditions, which go through the script's launches point by point for part (A) and mention set_stream only for point 9, could say that for these launches the claim relies on randn having finished (point 1), since the source's own code makes it plausible that it has not.

findings.summary: README 'Covered in particular' says every shape with n_cols ≤ 2^14 and n_rows below 2^31 − num_programs; in_off, out_off also bound n_rows (≤ 131073 rows of stride 16384)
findings.detail: README, Conditions, 'Covered in particular: … every other shape with n_cols ≤ 2^14 and n_rows below 2^31 − num_programs'. Inst.ok also has in_off and out_off ((n_rows − 1)·stride < 2^31) and x_len, y_len: a contiguous x of 16384 columns is covered only up to 131073 rows. The table above it states these fields correctly; the sentence could add 'and (n_rows − 1)·stride < 2^31' so that it does not overstate the coverage.

notes: Non-blocking: relTol is stated at BLOCK_SIZE, not n_cols; adding +0 is exact, so the sum's error depth is at most n_cols − 1 non-trivial additions, and a bound in n_cols would be tighter for instances with n_cols much below BLOCK_SIZE (the host's next_power_of_2 keeps them within a factor 2).
